title: AuthN key propagation latency and audit ingestion gap — postmortem
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a scheduled KMS signing-key rollout, a small propagation lag between the central key registry and edge validation services resulted in SSO validation failures and a related delay in audit-log ingestion. The incident lasted ~27 minutes for affected sessions before automated retries and an emergency fallback restored normal traffic. This ticket captures the postmortem findings, decisions, and action items to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: At 2026-02-23T18:12Z a key-rotation job published a new signing key version. Sidecar key caches in several edge regions failed to refresh due to an intermittent race between the key notification service and the service-mesh health check; this caused <1% of SSO token validations to reject during 18:12–18:39Z. Concurrently, audit-ingest workers dropped ~2,900 events because the ingress signature check failed and the ingestion retry logic treated them as unrecoverable. No customer data was exfiltrated. Several internal dashboards showed increased 5xxs and SSO latency spikes.
timeline: 18:11Z: Scheduled KMS key promotion started (rolling update)
18:12Z: Key registry wrote new version V+1 and broadcast notification
18:13Z: Edge sidecars attempted refresh; ~20% returned stale keystore due to cache TTL + mesh restart ordering
18:15Z: SSO auth failures detected by synthetic checks; alert SEV2 triggered
18:18Z: On-call paged; initial mitigation toggled to increase retry window for auth service
18:23Z: Audit-ingest pipeline reported signature validation errors; retries failing with 'unknown-key' classification
18:29Z: Emergency fallback deployed to allow validation with last-known-good key for 30s window (temporary mitigation)
18:39Z: Propagation completed; sidecars refreshed; error rates returned to baseline
18:45Z: Audit-ingest backfill job reprocessed failed events and confirmed ingestion for 2,900 events
19:10Z: Incident declared resolved; post-incident review scheduled
root_cause: A combination of factors: (1) the key-notification service broadcasts were not strongly ordered against the sidecar restart sequence in the service mesh, allowing a race where a new version existed but sidecars reloaded an older file before receiving the push; (2) the keystore cache TTL and mesh lifecycle hooks were misaligned; (3) audit-ingest classified 'unknown-key' as unrecoverable on first failure instead of enqueueing for a short-delay recheck.
impact: SSO token validation failed for a subset of users and internal services, resulting in elevated 5xx errors and degraded experience for some login flows for ~27 minutes. Approximately 2,900 audit events were temporarily dropped from the live ingestion stream and required backfill. No customer secrets or unencrypted data were exposed.
mitigations: Rolled out immediate fallback to accept last-known-good key for a bounded window (approved emergency change)
Backfilled failed audit events via audit-ingest backfill job; confirmed ingestion and checksum match
Increased monitoring sensitivity for key propagation latency and SSO validation error rate
action_items: (OWNED) Implement monotonic key versioning metadata (sequence numbers + publish timestamp) so services can detect out-of-order propagation — Owner: Ethan Chen — due 2026-03-10
(OWNED) Add a 'key-propagation-latency' metric and an alert at 10s median + 90th percentile thresholds across regions — Owner: Priya Nambiar — due 2026-03-05
(OWNED) Modify audit-ingest to treat 'unknown-key' as transient for 3 retry attempts with exponential backoff before marking unrecoverable — Owner: Marco Alvarez — due 2026-03-08
(OWNED) Add service-mesh lifecycle hook to defer sidecar keystore load until after key-notification handshake completes (or fallback to pull on startup) — Owner: Kelsey Moore — due 2026-03-15
(OWNED) Add chaos test to CI that simulates key rotation ordering races and validates auth + ingest resilience — Owner: SRE Team (nominal: Jordan Lee) — due 2026-04-01
(OWNED) Update runbook: include explicit emergency fallback steps, verification queries, and communication checklist for audit-log backfill — Owner: Aisha Patel — due 2026-03-03
decision_log: Do not change KMS rotation cadence immediately; root cause is propagation ordering not frequency (accepted)
Adopt bounded last-known-good key fallback for emergency windows but require audit of each use (accepted)
Prioritize metrics and retry logic changes before mesh lifecycle changes; mesh changes are medium-risk and scheduled after metrics are in place (accepted)
Require security review on any fallback that enlarges validation acceptance window (accepted)
postmortem_notes: This incident highlighted an operational blind spot: we had no single, observable signal that tied key publication to sidecar readiness. Our short-term emergency change introduced a bounded acceptance window which must be strictly audited. The long-term fix will be a mix of protocol-level monotonic keys, improved startup handshakes in the mesh, and more conservative audit-ingest retry semantics.
